facts.text: On this date in 1879, Edison successfully tested his first practical incandescent bulb — but the carbon filament he used came from bamboo sourced in Japan, making it a global product from day one.
On this date in 1966, a coal tip collapsed onto the Welsh village of Aberfan, killing 116 children. The UK government took 50 years to repay the disaster fund it had raided from the survivors.

Mongolia has more horses than people — roughly 4.2 million horses to 3.4 million humans — and about a third of the population still lives nomadically, moving with their herds across an area larger than Western Europe.
The city of Istanbul spans two continents, but it also spans three seas: the Black Sea, the Sea of Marmara, and the Aegean are all reachable within its municipal boundaries.

Lesotho is one of only three countries in the world entirely surrounded by a single other country — and at an average elevation above 1,400 meters, it is the only nation on Earth where all inhabited land sits that high.
On this day in 1987, global markets were still reeling from Black Monday — the Dow had shed 22.6% two days earlier, the largest single-day percentage crash in US history, dwarfing even 1929.
On Oct 21, 1929, a brief market rally fooled investors into thinking the worst was over. Four days later, Black Thursday erased the optimism entirely.
The New York Stock Exchange was founded under a buttonwood tree in 1792. The original agreement was signed by 24 brokers — the entire industry fit on one sheet of paper.
Saudi Aramco's 2019 IPO raised $25.6 billion, making it the largest in history. It briefly gave the company a $2 trillion valuation — more than Apple, Microsoft, and Google combined at the time.

The Dutch East India Company, the world's first publicly traded company, was so large at its 1637 peak that its inflation-adjusted value exceeded $8 trillion — more than today's five largest companies combined.
On this day in 1879, Edison demonstrated a working incandescent bulb — but the filament was carbonized cotton thread, not tungsten. Tungsten only replaced it three decades later.
Your skeleton is not static. Every 10 years, virtually all your bone mass has been silently dissolved and rebuilt, atom by atom.
On this day in 1879, while Edison lit his lab, the universe was already 13.8 billion years old and utterly indifferent to the occasion.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Mantis shrimp see 16 types of color receptors compared to the human three — yet research shows they are worse at distinguishing similar hues, processing color locally rather than comparatively.
On this day in 1879, Edison first successfully tested his incandescent bulb — younger technology than the photograph, which Niepce had captured 52 years earlier.
Oxford University was teaching students when the Aztec Empire didn't yet exist. Oxford dates to 1096; the Aztecs founded Tenochtitlan in 1325.
On this day in 1879, the same week Edison lit his bulb, Dostoevsky was still alive, Nietzsche was publishing, and Tolstoy had just finished Anna Karenina. Modernity arrived in a crowd.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died in 30 BC; Giza was finished around 2560 BC.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, and a full 134 years before the first commercially sold personal computer.
Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): the wordless look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. One word for a feeling most languages need a paragraph to describe.
Sonder (coined 2012, Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows): the realization that every stranger has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Too new to be old, too true to be ignored.

On this day in 1879, Edison successfully tested a working incandescent bulb. The word 'electricity' predates him by 230 years, from Latin 'electricus' — meaning 'like amber,' which sparks when rubbed.
On this day in 1879, the word 'filament' entered everyday speech almost overnight. It comes from Latin 'filum,' thread — the same root as 'file,' as in a line of people, and 'profile.'

Hiraeth (Welsh): a longing for a home that no longer exists, or perhaps never did. Untranslatable not because Welsh is strange, but because English has never admitted that grief deserves its own word.
On this date in 2021, Shiba Inu's market cap briefly surpassed Ford and Twitter. It had no revenue, no product, and was cloned from Dogecoin's open-source code in an afternoon.
On this date in 2015, Ethereum processed its first non-test mainnet transaction — Vitalik paying himself 0 ETH to confirm the chain was live.
Bitcoin's timechain has never produced exactly one block per ten minutes. The true median interval is closer to 9.6 minutes, because difficulty adjusts to hashrate averages, not moments.
The DAO hack in 2016 didn't exploit a bug in Ethereum. It exploited a bug in one contract written on Ethereum — a distinction the community then ignored when justifying the hard fork.
Satoshi's genesis block coinbase contains the text 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not as metadata, but permanently embedded in the raw transaction input script.

On this date in 2015, Google DeepMind published its Nature paper on Deep Q-Networks beating human experts at 49 Atari games — the first system to learn control policies directly from raw pixels across diverse tasks.

Today in 2022, Stability AI released Stable Diffusion publicly, shifting image generation from API-gated curiosity to local, uncensored infrastructure running on consumer GPUs within 72 hours of launch.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US households, for a single model checkpoint.
The transformer architecture, now foundational to nearly every frontier model, was published in 2017 by eight authors — six of whom have since left Google, most to found competing AI labs.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins before most structural biologists had published a dozen. The entire UniProt database went from ~17% covered to effectively complete in under two years.
